assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray burst afterglows with BeppoSAX and the optical and radio follow-up settled a thirty-year debate and showed that bursts are cosmological. This was an instrument-enabled discovery: a wide-field X-ray camera paired with a narrow-field telescope, giving arcminute positions fast enough for ground-based follow-up. It opened a whole field and still underpins GRB, supernova-connection and transient astronomy.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB instrumentation and the first X-ray afterglow (GRB 970228). Kulkarni's group delivered the key redshift and radio/optical work that fixed the cosmological distance. The three-name configuration seems defensible. Others (e.g. van Paradijs, Groot, Metzger, Djorgovski, Piro) have strong claims; the longlist credit does not cover them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently many times over about three decades, with the interpretation stable (cosmological distances, relativistic fireball). Recognition is, if anything, overdue, and van Paradijs has died, which limits the credit problem.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied three names fully capture decisive credit, given the optical-counterpart discovery and the large BeppoSAX team.
I have not independently checked the exact priority dates and roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy: a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice, a major instrumental achievement, followed by the discovery of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux (2013), the TXS 0506+056 association (2018) and the Galactic-plane neutrinos (2023). It is an astroparticle result of the type I know best, with a real new observational window.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the only credited name and is widely seen as the originator and leader of IceCube. A single-laureate prize under-represents a large collaboration and the AMANDA precursor, and the credited list offers no other name to share it with, so the configuration is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses, but source identification is still incomplete; the TXS association is about 3 sigma and the Galactic plane result is recent. Recognition is plausible but arguably not fully mature.
uncertainties: Only one credited name, so credit configuration is thin and may be contested.
Source-level confirmation is limited; KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD provide only partial independent checks so far.
I have not verified the current significance levels.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs discovery rests on the conception and construction of two detectors of unprecedented scale and complexity. As a detector builder I think the instrument achievement deserves recognition in its own right. The 2013 prize went to the theory; the experimental side has never been honoured.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are the founding spokespersons or proposers of CMS and ATLAS. This fits a three-person prize reasonably well, but it singles out leaders over thousands of collaborators, and others (e.g. Gianotti, Incandela, Tonelli) also played decisive roles.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed; the Higgs properties are measured with growing precision. A prize now would be timely, and the Committee has already honoured the underlying physics.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee would reward detector conception and leadership rather than the discovery itself, given the size of the collaborations.
Allocation among the many possible leaders is contested and not resolved by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach 10^-18 fractional uncertainty. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice, and the clocks now enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. This is precision measurement at its best, with careful control of systematics.
assessment.attribution: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's experimental development, with the Sr clock and the comb link, form a clean two-laureate configuration. Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) were already honoured for neighbouring work, but this is distinct.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced in several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others). The redefinition of the second is pending but the physics is established.
uncertainties: Other contributors to optical lattice clocks (e.g. Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom, Lemonde, Schiller) might be argued to share credit.
Overlap with the earlier Nobel prizes for precision spectroscopy and ion clocks could be argued.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonova theory and the observation of AT2017gfo with GW170817 established neutron-star mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis and linked gravitational waves to electromagnetic light. Scientifically important and connecting nuclear physics, astrophysics and multimessenger observation.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and Kasen made the central theoretical predictions, and Foley led a team that was among the first to detect the optical counterpart. The credit is complicated: Li and Paczynski (1998) proposed the original idea, Coulter and the Swope team, Lattimer and Schramm, and many others are relevant. This is a compound discovery whose parts might need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Based on one well-observed event, with the r-process interpretation supported but not fully settled. GW detection was already recognised in 2017. Somewhat premature until further events.
uncertainties: A single multimessenger event limits independent confirmation.
The fraction of r-process material produced by mergers versus other sites remains open.
Disputed priority and a very large collaboration make the three names uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire flat-band field, which has had a very large impact. Outside my own expertise; I rely on colleagues for the condensed-matter judgement.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative flat-band prediction at the magic angle. Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental discovery. The pairing of theory with experiment is clean. Others who might be argued to share credit include Cao, Dean, Young, Mele and Santos.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups within a few years and the field is growing, but the microscopic mechanism of superconductivity is not settled, so the physics may not have reached a stable interpretation.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity remains open.
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on the relative importance versus other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP made precision cosmology possible, with percent-level cosmological parameters, and fixed the standard LambdaCDM model. The instrument was a careful differential radiometer design, with systematic control which I find impressive.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel led the cosmological analysis and Page led the instrument design. A fair configuration, but it neglects the large WMAP team and the COBE and Planck lineage. The 2006 prize recognised COBE, and the 2019 prize recognised theoretical cosmology.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by Planck, ACT and SPT. The timing is very late and the novelty relative to earlier CMB prizes is reduced.
uncertainties: Planck largely superseded WMAP, which lowers the case for a stand-alone WMAP prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry underpins precision tests of gravity and the equivalence principle, gravimetry and inertial sensing. The instrumentation is a real achievement; the techniques are widely used and the field has maturing applications to sensing.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich contributed foundational demonstrations and the high-precision gravimeter and gyroscope work, with Chu (1997) and Ramsey earlier. Schmiedmayer and others, and Chu's own work, complicate credit; four names are supplied and only three can be chosen.
assessment.maturity: Well established, reproduced widely, and moving toward field use. The fundamental-physics reach (equivalence principle, G, the fine-structure constant) is still improving and no single decisive result stands out.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over a large community, including those already honoured in 1997.
The headline discovery is less sharply defined than in other candidates.
